findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the `?` suffix, so the inclusion guard never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` (with a question mark) to decide whether to include an attribute. The method defined here is `include_website_name`, so it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized (as `null` when the user has no website). Rename to `include_website_name?` so the guard actually takes effect.

findings.title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking website for TL0 users seen by anonymous
findings.body: `website` is listed under `untrusted_attributes` and is suppressed when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user viewed anonymously). `website_name` is a plain attribute and is derived from the same value, so the site/host (and path) is still exposed to anonymous visitors, defeating the restriction. The existing spec 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' does not cover `website_name`. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and to the spec list.

findings.title: String mutation with `<<` on a literal can raise under frozen string literals
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` mutates the `"."` literal in place. If frozen string literals are ever enabled (magic comment or newer Ruby default), this raises FrozenError. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host` instead.

findings.title: URL is parsed repeatedly and only the first parse is guarded; query/fragment dropped
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is evaluated up to three times per call and only the first is protected by `rescue nil`. Parse once into a local variable. Also only `.host + .path` is used, so any query string or fragment in the user's website URL is silently dropped from the displayed name, which can be misleading when the full path is intentionally shown.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic shows full path for unrelated domains of equal label count
findings.body: The `elsif` branch only requires that the hostnames have the same number of labels (>2) and share all labels after the first. So e.g. website `evil.example.com` with instance `forum.example.com` is treated as 'same site' and the full path is rendered, and conversely `forum.example.com` with instance `example.com` (reverse of the documented case) only yields the host. The matching rules should be based on the registrable domain, and the asymmetry deserves a test.
